1	# DevDesk Backlog
2	
3	**Last Updated:** 2026-08-02
4	
5	Open work for DevDesk: known defects, technical debt, and planned features.
6	Replaces the former `todo.md` at the repository root. Items completed there
7	(network topology visualisation, inter-container ping/curl) have been dropped
8	rather than carried over.
9	
10	---
11	
12	## 1. Known defects
13	
14	D1, D3 and D6 — the byte-vs-rune lot — were fixed together; see
15	[§1.1](#11-fixed). The remainder is unfixed and reachable from the current code.
16	
17	### D2 — The "permanent delete" checkbox is documented as locked but is not
18	
19	`internal/ui/components/delete_confirm_modal.go:35` and `:99-105`
20	
21	`NewDeleteConfirmModalPermanent` pre-checks *Immediate deletion* and its doc
22	comment states the box is non-modifiable ("pré-cochée et non modifiable"). Nothing
23	enforces that: `space` and `enter` on the checkbox still toggle it.
24	
25	A project already marked for deletion can therefore be sent through a
26	grace-period delete that the caller does not expect. Pinned by
27	`TestDeleteConfirmModalPermanentCheckboxIsStillToggleable`.
28	
29	**Fix:** carry a `locked` flag on the modal and make the toggle a no-op when set,
30	or drop the claim from the doc comment.
31	
32	### D4 — `DeleteConfirmModal` uses `Tab` for field navigation
33	
34	`internal/ui/components/delete_confirm_modal.go:89-97`
35	
36	`tab` / `shift+tab` cycle checkbox → Yes → No. Rule 135 reserves those keys for
37	tab switching and assigns field navigation to `↑ / ↓` exclusively.
38	
39	Cosmetic in isolation, but it is the kind of inconsistency Rule 135 exists to
40	prevent. Changing it alters muscle memory, so it needs a deliberate call rather
41	than a drive-by fix.
42	
43	### D5 — Unreachable focus clamp in `CreationForm`
44	
45	`internal/ui/components/creation_form.go:221-223`
46	
47	After cycling the resource type, the code clamps `focusedField` down to
48	`maxField()`. The surrounding branch only runs when `focusedField == 0`, and
49	`maxField()` is never below 4, so the clamp can never fire.
50	
51	Dead defensive code. Harmless, but it implies a state transition that cannot
52	happen and is misleading to read.
53	
54	### D7 — `extractTarGz` keeps parent references in archive paths
55	
56	`internal/oci/oci.go:262`
57	
58	Extraction strips leading `./` and `/` but does not reject `..`, so an archive
59	member named `../../etc/passwd` survives as a map key containing parent
60	references.
61	
62	**Not exploitable today.** The sole consumer, `applyTemplate` in
63	`internal/ui/gitlab/explorer/model.go:1053`, turns the map into GitLab commit
64	actions rather than writing to disk, and the server validates the paths.
65	
66	Recorded because the hazard is latent: any future caller that writes these keys
67	under a target directory inherits a Zip Slip. Pinned by
68	`TestExtractTarGzPreservesParentTraversalInKeys`.
69	
70	**Fix:** reject entries whose cleaned path escapes the root, before returning
71	them.
72	
73	### 1.1 Fixed
74	
75	**D1** (`ReportModal.View()` emitted invalid UTF-8), **D3** (`wrapInputLines`
76	looped forever when `wrapWidth <= 0`) and **D6** (`wordWrap` measured bytes) were
77	fixed together, since D1 and D6 were the same byte-vs-rune defect.
78	
79	Rather than patch each call site, the truncation logic moved into
80	`internal/ui/theme/text.go` per Rule 117: `StringWidth`, `TruncateWidth` (keeps
81	the head) and `TruncateTailWidth` (keeps the tail, for paths). All three measure
82	terminal columns, so double-width glyphs are handled too, not just multibyte
83	ones.
84	
85	A **fourth site carried the same defect** and was not recorded here: `truncate`
86	in `internal/ui/security/model.go` sliced bytes exactly like D1 and rendered
87	Trivy finding titles. It is now `theme.TruncateWidth` and the local helper is
88	gone.
89	
90	The two pinned tests that `t.Skip()`d became real assertions
91	(`TestReportModalViewKeepsMultibyteRunesIntact`,
92	`TestWordWrapMeasuresColumnsNotBytes`).
93	
94	One call site was deliberately left alone: `truncateResultLine` in
95	`internal/ui/oci_resources/connectivity_form.go` counts runes rather than bytes,
96	so it is correct — merely imprecise on double-width glyphs. Folding it into the
97	theme helpers is a cleanup, not a defect fix.
98	
99	**Context isolation in `GitCredentialStorage` never worked.** Found while
100	planning the coverage work, not previously recorded.
101	
102	The three methods carried the DevDesk context in the `path` field of the git
103	credential protocol (`path=devdesk/context/<name>`). Git discards that field
104	unless `credential.useHttpPath` is set, which is off by default, so every
105	credential was keyed on `protocol://host` alone. Two contexts pointing at the
106	same GitLab host silently overwrote each other, and the last one to authenticate
107	won for all of them. Verified against a real `git credential` store before and
108	after the fix; it affects every helper (GCM, wincred, osxkeychain), since git
109	strips the path before the helper is ever called.
110	
111	**Fix:** pass `-c credential.useHttpPath=true` on each invocation. Scoping it to
112	the call leaves the user's git configuration alone — setting it globally would
113	change credential resolution for every repository on the machine. Pinned by
114	`TestGitCredentialIsolatesContexts`.
115	
116	Existing users must re-authenticate: credentials saved under the old
117	path-stripped key no longer match. Those credentials were ambiguous across
118	contexts anyway.
119	
120	Two smaller defects went with it:
121	
122	- `Delete` had no timeout, while `Save` and `Load` bounded themselves to 2 s
123	  precisely so an unconfigured helper could not freeze the TUI. Logout could
124	  hang indefinitely.
125	- The timeout killed only the direct `git` child, though its comment claimed
126	  otherwise. The helper git spawns survives and holds the output pipes open, so
127	  `Run` kept blocking. All three calls now share one `runCredential` helper built
128	  on `exec.CommandContext` plus `WaitDelay`, which bounds the wait on those pipes.
129	
130	`internal/credentials/helper.go` (`HelperStorage`, 137 lines) was deleted rather
131	than fixed: nothing outside its own tests constructed it. It was also broken —
132	`detectHelper()` returns whatever `git config credential.helper` holds, so a
133	common value like `store --file=/path` became the single unfindable command
134	`credential-store --file=/path` — and it hardcoded `protocol=https`, unlike
135	`GitCredentialStorage`, which reads the scheme from the URL.
136	
137	---
138	
139	## 2. Technical debt
140	
141	### Test coverage
142	
143	Currently **18.2 %** overall; the agreed target is 80 %, which needs roughly
144	**+7 250 covered statements** over today's ~2 100.
145	
146	Phased plan, with the harness and most of phase 1 delivered:
147	
148	| Phase | Scope | Status |
149	|---|---|---|
150	| 0 | `internal/ui/testutil` Bubble Tea harness | **done** (100 %) |
151	| 1 | Leaf components and pure helpers | **done** except the `ui/theme` complement (~55 stmts) |
152	| 2 | Mid-size view state machines (`status`, `containers`, `dashboard`, `gitlab/auth`) | pending (~1 240 stmts) |
153	| 3 | Large views (`workspaces`, `explorer`, `security`, `netdiag`) | pending (~2 470 stmts) |
154	| 4 | `ui/oci_resources` | pending (~1 995 stmts) |
155	| 5 | Router and I/O seams (`app`, `scan`, `docker`) | pending (~1 360 stmts) |
156	| 6 | Remainder to reach 80 % | pending (~400 stmts) |
157	
158	Phase 1 progress:
159	
160	| Package | Before | Now |
161	|---|---|---|
162	| `internal/ui/testutil` | — | **100 %** (new) |
163	| `internal/ui/shortcut` | 0 % | **100 %** |
164	| `internal/ui/help` | 0 % | **96.7 %** |
165	| `internal/ui/components` | 0 % | **79.8 %** |
166	| `internal/oci` | 0 % | **33.6 %** |
167	| `internal/docker` | 7.3 % | **65.4 %** (phase 5, pulled forward — see below) |
168	| `internal/gitlab` | 7.5 % | **100 %** |
169	| `internal/credentials` | 29.5 % | **98.2 %** |
170	
171	`internal/oci` stops at 33.6 % because the remaining statements are registry HTTP
172	paths (`DownloadTemplate`, `listCatalog`, `ListTemplates`) that need a fuller
173	`httptest` fixture — a manifest plus a gzipped layer — rather than the
174	single-response stubs used so far.
175	
176	Phase 5's blocker is cleared for `docker`: the package now routes every CLI
177	invocation through the `dockerRunner` seam in `internal/docker/exec.go`, so tests
178	drive argument building and output parsing against canned output. `scan` and
179	`app` remain.
180	
181	`internal/gitlab` needed no seam: every function takes a `*gitlabclient.Client`
182	built from a base URL, so an `httptest` server standing in for the API covers
183	the whole package. `Clone` is exercised against a throwaway local repository
184	rather than mocked, and skips when no `git` binary is on `PATH`.
185	
186	`internal/credentials` needed no seam either. `git credential` is steerable
187	through the environment, so the tests redirect `HOME`, `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` and
188	`GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM` at a temporary directory and run the real binary against a
189	throwaway `store` helper — nothing reaches the developer's keychain. Running the
190	real git is what surfaced the context-isolation defect recorded in §1.1; a stub
191	would have frozen the broken behaviour instead. The 2 s timeout is covered by
192	installing a credential helper that sleeps.
193	
194	### Files over the 800-line ceiling
195	
196	The project's own coding rules cap files at 800 lines. Seven exceed it:
197	
198	| File | Lines |
199	|---|---|
200	| `internal/ui/security/model.go` | 1785 |
201	| `internal/ui/oci_resources/update.go` | 1556 |
202	| `internal/app/app.go` | 1333 |
203	| `internal/ui/gitlab/explorer/model.go` | 1214 |
204	| `internal/ui/workspaces/model.go` | 1133 |
205	| `internal/ui/netdiag/model.go` | 995 |
206	| `internal/ui/oci_resources/registry_browser.go` | 822 |
207	
208	`internal/docker/client.go` (1176 lines — the 1069 recorded earlier was stale)
209	was split into `exec.go`, `containers.go`, `images.go`, `networks.go`,
210	`volumes.go`, `registry.go`, `launch.go`, `system.go` and `parse.go`; the largest
211	is now 269 lines. The former `network.go` became `ports.go`, since it reports the
212	host's listening sockets via `ss` rather than Docker networks — the name was
213	free for the `docker network` family.
214	
215	This interacts with the coverage work: writing several thousand statements of
216	tests against these files before splitting them freezes their current structure.
217	Decide the order deliberately. Splitting `docker` first was the cheap case — its
218	7.3 % coverage meant almost no tests were pinned to the old shape.
219	
220	### Race detector cannot run locally
221	
222	`mise run test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler on `PATH`. Without one
223	it fails with `cgo: C compiler "gcc" not found`. Bubble Tea `Cmd`s run
224	concurrently, so this is the check most likely to catch a Rule 110 violation.
225	
226	**Now covered by CI.** `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `mise run test-race` on
227	every push and pull request, on `ubuntu-latest`, which has a toolchain. The first
228	run reported no data race across all 17 packages.
229	
230	That is a baseline, not a clean bill of health: the detector only sees code the
231	tests actually execute, and coverage is 18.2 %. Rule 110 violations in untested
232	paths — most of the view layer — remain invisible. The two efforts compound, so
233	this is an argument for the coverage phases rather than a substitute for them.
234	
235	Installing a local toolchain is still worth doing for anyone touching `Cmd`s, to
236	avoid learning about a race from CI after the fact.
237	
238	---
239	
240	## 3. Planned features
241	
242	Carried over from `todo.md`.
243	
244	### 3.1 Network diagnostics
245	
246	- **Port-forwarding manager** — an interactive dashboard to manage port
247	  redirections to the host machine.
248	
249	### 3.2 Interactive security remediation
250	
251	- **Auto-patch assistance** — after a Trivy scan, offer to generate a patch or an
252	  updated `Dockerfile` that bumps the base image version to clear critical CVEs.
253	- **Local SAST** — wire security linters (Gitleaks for secrets, IaC linters)
254	  directly into the Workspace view.
255	
256	### 3.3 OCI build and cache analyser
257	
258	- **Layer visualisation** — analyse a local image and show the size of each
259	  layer, in the spirit of `dive`. Intended approach:
260	  - Integrated via `google/go-containerregistry` ("daemonless", no dependency on
261	    the Docker daemon).
262	  - Talk to OCI registries directly, pulling manifests and configs without
263	    downloading the whole image.
264	  - Stream layers in memory (`tar`) to rebuild the filesystem tree.
265	  - Compute wasted space by detecting whiteout files (`.wh.`).
266	- **Cache-miss analysis** — explain why a build's cache was invalidated, e.g.
267	  "`package.json` changed, invalidating the cache".
268	
269	### 3.4 Spontaneous dev containers
270	
271	- **Configuration injection** — inject the developer's dotfiles (vim, zsh,
272	  aliases) when opening a terminal inside a container.
273	- **Hot volume mount** — mount the current working directory into a running
274	  container on the fly, to test a local script without rebuilding the image.
275	
276	### 3.5 Resource dashboard (embedded mini-htop)
277	
278	- **TUI charts** — braille-character charts showing live CPU, RAM and network I/O
279	  for every container in the selected project.
280	- **Visual alerts** — user-defined thresholds (e.g. memory saturation).
281	
282	### 3.6 GitHub support alongside GitLab, one active forge per context
283	
284	Support GitHub as well as GitLab, with **exactly one backend active per
285	configuration context**. A context targets one forge; switching forge means
286	switching context.
287	
288	Not started. The notes below are what the current code imposes on the design,
289	not a chosen design.
290	
291	#### What is coupled to GitLab today
292	
293	| Surface | Size |
294	|---|---|
295	| `internal/gitlab` + `internal/ui/gitlab/{auth,explorer}` | ~3 900 lines |
296	| Direct uses of `*gitlabclient.Client` outside `internal/gitlab` | 66, across 8 files |
297	
298	The concrete SDK type leaks into `internal/shared/state.go:57`
299	(`GitLabClient *gitlabclient.Client`), so every consumer is bound to go-gitlab
300	rather than to a DevDesk abstraction. That field is the load-bearing change: an
301	interface there is what makes a second forge possible at all.
302	
303	Also GitLab-shaped: `GitLabConfig` in `internal/config/config.go:41` (URL, token,
304	clone method, pull settings), the `gitlab-auth` / `gitlab-explorer` view names
305	and their `gla` / `gle` aliases in `internal/command/parser.go`, and
306	`shared.GitLabStats`.
307	
308	#### Model mismatches to settle before coding
309	
310	These are not implementation details; they decide what the abstraction can even
311	promise.
312	
313	- **Nesting.** The explorer is a tree of groups → subgroups → projects. GitHub
314	  has no nested groups: an organisation holds repositories, flat. Either the
315	  tree degrades to two levels for GitHub, or the abstraction exposes a depth the
316	  backend declares.
317	- **Deletion.** `DeleteGroup` / `DeleteProject` implement GitLab's two-step
318	  permanent delete (schedule, then purge under the renamed
319	  `-deletion_scheduled-<id>` path). GitHub deletes immediately and has no
320	  equivalent, so the "permanent" checkbox is meaningless there — see also D2.
321	- **Dashboard counters.** `FetchDashboardStats` reads `X-Total` from five list
322	  endpoints. GitHub has no equivalent header for these; the counts come from the
323	  search API (`search/issues?q=is:open+is:pr+assignee:@me`), with different rate
324	  limits and semantics.
325	- **Vocabulary.** Group/project/merge request vs organisation/repository/pull
326	  request. The UI must pick per-backend labels or a neutral vocabulary; Rule 129
327	  applies either way.
328	
329	#### Open decision: Go SDKs or the `gh` / `glab` CLIs
330	
331	Worth deciding before any code is written, because it determines whether the
332	package needs a seam.
333	
334	Arguments for the CLIs:
335	
336	- Authentication is already solved, including OAuth device flow, self-hosted
337	  hosts and token storage. DevDesk's own credential handling could shrink — and
338	  it has already proven fragile (see §1.1).
339	- `gh api` and `glab api` are raw REST/GraphQL passthroughs, so no SDK is needed
340	  for coverage of endpoints the abstraction does not model.
341	- No SDK version churn to track for two forges.
342	
343	Arguments against:
344

# DevDesk Backlog

**Last Updated:** 2026-08-02

Open work for DevDesk: known defects, technical debt, and planned features.
Replaces the former `todo.md` at the repository root. Items completed there
(network topology visualisation, inter-container ping/curl) have been dropped
rather than carried over.

---

## 1. Known defects

D1, D3 and D6 — the byte-vs-rune lot — were fixed together; see
[§1.1](#11-fixed). The remainder is unfixed and reachable from the current code.

### D2 — The "permanent delete" checkbox is documented as locked but is not

`internal/ui/components/delete_confirm_modal.go:35` and `:99-105`

`NewDeleteConfirmModalPermanent` pre-checks *Immediate deletion* and its doc
comment states the box is non-modifiable ("pré-cochée et non modifiable"). Nothing
enforces that: `space` and `enter` on the checkbox still toggle it.

A project already marked for deletion can therefore be sent through a
grace-period delete that the caller does not expect. Pinned by
`TestDeleteConfirmModalPermanentCheckboxIsStillToggleable`.

**Fix:** carry a `locked` flag on the modal and make the toggle a no-op when set,
or drop the claim from the doc comment.

### D4 — `DeleteConfirmModal` uses `Tab` for field navigation

`internal/ui/components/delete_confirm_modal.go:89-97`

`tab` / `shift+tab` cycle checkbox → Yes → No. Rule 135 reserves those keys for
tab switching and assigns field navigation to `↑ / ↓` exclusively.

Cosmetic in isolation, but it is the kind of inconsistency Rule 135 exists to
prevent. Changing it alters muscle memory, so it needs a deliberate call rather
than a drive-by fix.

### D5 — Unreachable focus clamp in `CreationForm`

`internal/ui/components/creation_form.go:221-223`

After cycling the resource type, the code clamps `focusedField` down to
`maxField()`. The surrounding branch only runs when `focusedField == 0`, and
`maxField()` is never below 4, so the clamp can never fire.

Dead defensive code. Harmless, but it implies a state transition that cannot
happen and is misleading to read.

### D7 — `extractTarGz` keeps parent references in archive paths

`internal/oci/oci.go:262`

Extraction strips leading `./` and `/` but does not reject `..`, so an archive
member named `../../etc/passwd` survives as a map key containing parent
references.

**Not exploitable today.** The sole consumer, `applyTemplate` in
`internal/ui/gitlab/explorer/model.go:1053`, turns the map into GitLab commit
actions rather than writing to disk, and the server validates the paths.

Recorded because the hazard is latent: any future caller that writes these keys
under a target directory inherits a Zip Slip. Pinned by
`TestExtractTarGzPreservesParentTraversalInKeys`.

**Fix:** reject entries whose cleaned path escapes the root, before returning
them.

### 1.1 Fixed

**D1** (`ReportModal.View()` emitted invalid UTF-8), **D3** (`wrapInputLines`
looped forever when `wrapWidth <= 0`) and **D6** (`wordWrap` measured bytes) were
fixed together, since D1 and D6 were the same byte-vs-rune defect.

Rather than patch each call site, the truncation logic moved into
`internal/ui/theme/text.go` per Rule 117: `StringWidth`, `TruncateWidth` (keeps
the head) and `TruncateTailWidth` (keeps the tail, for paths). All three measure
terminal columns, so double-width glyphs are handled too, not just multibyte
ones.

A **fourth site carried the same defect** and was not recorded here: `truncate`
in `internal/ui/security/model.go` sliced bytes exactly like D1 and rendered
Trivy finding titles. It is now `theme.TruncateWidth` and the local helper is
gone.

The two pinned tests that `t.Skip()`d became real assertions
(`TestReportModalViewKeepsMultibyteRunesIntact`,
`TestWordWrapMeasuresColumnsNotBytes`).

One call site was deliberately left alone: `truncateResultLine` in
`internal/ui/oci_resources/connectivity_form.go` counts runes rather than bytes,
so it is correct — merely imprecise on double-width glyphs. Folding it into the
theme helpers is a cleanup, not a defect fix.

**Context isolation in `GitCredentialStorage` never worked.** Found while
planning the coverage work, not previously recorded.

The three methods carried the DevDesk context in the `path` field of the git
credential protocol (`path=devdesk/context/<name>`). Git discards that field
unless `credential.useHttpPath` is set, which is off by default, so every
credential was keyed on `protocol://host` alone. Two contexts pointing at the
same GitLab host silently overwrote each other, and the last one to authenticate
won for all of them. Verified against a real `git credential` store before and
after the fix; it affects every helper (GCM, wincred, osxkeychain), since git
strips the path before the helper is ever called.

**Fix:** pass `-c credential.useHttpPath=true` on each invocation. Scoping it to
the call leaves the user's git configuration alone — setting it globally would
change credential resolution for every repository on the machine. Pinned by
`TestGitCredentialIsolatesContexts`.

Existing users must re-authenticate: credentials saved under the old
path-stripped key no longer match. Those credentials were ambiguous across
contexts anyway.

Two smaller defects went with it:

- `Delete` had no timeout, while `Save` and `Load` bounded themselves to 2 s
  precisely so an unconfigured helper could not freeze the TUI. Logout could
  hang indefinitely.
- The timeout killed only the direct `git` child, though its comment claimed
  otherwise. The helper git spawns survives and holds the output pipes open, so
  `Run` kept blocking. All three calls now share one `runCredential` helper built
  on `exec.CommandContext` plus `WaitDelay`, which bounds the wait on those pipes.

`internal/credentials/helper.go` (`HelperStorage`, 137 lines) was deleted rather
than fixed: nothing outside its own tests constructed it. It was also broken —
`detectHelper()` returns whatever `git config credential.helper` holds, so a
common value like `store --file=/path` became the single unfindable command
`credential-store --file=/path` — and it hardcoded `protocol=https`, unlike
`GitCredentialStorage`, which reads the scheme from the URL.

---

## 2. Technical debt

### Test coverage

Currently **18.2 %** overall; the agreed target is 80 %, which needs roughly
**+7 250 covered statements** over today's ~2 100.

Phased plan, with the harness and most of phase 1 delivered:

| Phase | Scope | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `internal/ui/testutil` Bubble Tea harness | **done** (100 %) |
| 1 | Leaf components and pure helpers | **done** except the `ui/theme` complement (~55 stmts) |
| 2 | Mid-size view state machines (`status`, `containers`, `dashboard`, `gitlab/auth`) | pending (~1 240 stmts) |
| 3 | Large views (`workspaces`, `explorer`, `security`, `netdiag`) | pending (~2 470 stmts) |
| 4 | `ui/oci_resources` | pending (~1 995 stmts) |
| 5 | Router and I/O seams (`app`, `scan`, `docker`) | pending (~1 360 stmts) |
| 6 | Remainder to reach 80 % | pending (~400 stmts) |

Phase 1 progress:

| Package | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `internal/ui/testutil` | — | **100 %** (new) |
| `internal/ui/shortcut` | 0 % | **100 %** |
| `internal/ui/help` | 0 % | **96.7 %** |
| `internal/ui/components` | 0 % | **79.8 %** |
| `internal/oci` | 0 % | **33.6 %** |
| `internal/docker` | 7.3 % | **65.4 %** (phase 5, pulled forward — see below) |
| `internal/gitlab` | 7.5 % | **100 %** |
| `internal/credentials` | 29.5 % | **98.2 %** |

`internal/oci` stops at 33.6 % because the remaining statements are registry HTTP
paths (`DownloadTemplate`, `listCatalog`, `ListTemplates`) that need a fuller
`httptest` fixture — a manifest plus a gzipped layer — rather than the
single-response stubs used so far.

Phase 5's blocker is cleared for `docker`: the package now routes every CLI
invocation through the `dockerRunner` seam in `internal/docker/exec.go`, so tests
drive argument building and output parsing against canned output. `scan` and
`app` remain.

`internal/gitlab` needed no seam: every function takes a `*gitlabclient.Client`
built from a base URL, so an `httptest` server standing in for the API covers
the whole package. `Clone` is exercised against a throwaway local repository
rather than mocked, and skips when no `git` binary is on `PATH`.

`internal/credentials` needed no seam either. `git credential` is steerable
through the environment, so the tests redirect `HOME`, `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` and
`GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM` at a temporary directory and run the real binary against a
throwaway `store` helper — nothing reaches the developer's keychain. Running the
real git is what surfaced the context-isolation defect recorded in §1.1; a stub
would have frozen the broken behaviour instead. The 2 s timeout is covered by
installing a credential helper that sleeps.

### Files over the 800-line ceiling

The project's own coding rules cap files at 800 lines. Seven exceed it:

| File | Lines |
|---|---|
| `internal/ui/security/model.go` | 1785 |
| `internal/ui/oci_resources/update.go` | 1556 |
| `internal/app/app.go` | 1333 |
| `internal/ui/gitlab/explorer/model.go` | 1214 |
| `internal/ui/workspaces/model.go` | 1133 |
| `internal/ui/netdiag/model.go` | 995 |
| `internal/ui/oci_resources/registry_browser.go` | 822 |

`internal/docker/client.go` (1176 lines — the 1069 recorded earlier was stale)
was split into `exec.go`, `containers.go`, `images.go`, `networks.go`,
`volumes.go`, `registry.go`, `launch.go`, `system.go` and `parse.go`; the largest
is now 269 lines. The former `network.go` became `ports.go`, since it reports the
host's listening sockets via `ss` rather than Docker networks — the name was
free for the `docker network` family.

This interacts with the coverage work: writing several thousand statements of
tests against these files before splitting them freezes their current structure.
Decide the order deliberately. Splitting `docker` first was the cheap case — its
7.3 % coverage meant almost no tests were pinned to the old shape.

### Race detector cannot run locally

`mise run test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler on `PATH`. Without one
it fails with `cgo: C compiler "gcc" not found`. Bubble Tea `Cmd`s run
concurrently, so this is the check most likely to catch a Rule 110 violation.

**Now covered by CI.** `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `mise run test-race` on
every push and pull request, on `ubuntu-latest`, which has a toolchain. The first
run reported no data race across all 17 packages.

That is a baseline, not a clean bill of health: the detector only sees code the
tests actually execute, and coverage is 18.2 %. Rule 110 violations in untested
paths — most of the view layer — remain invisible. The two efforts compound, so
this is an argument for the coverage phases rather than a substitute for them.

Installing a local toolchain is still worth doing for anyone touching `Cmd`s, to
avoid learning about a race from CI after the fact.

---

## 3. Planned features

Carried over from `todo.md`.

### 3.1 Network diagnostics

- **Port-forwarding manager** — an interactive dashboard to manage port
  redirections to the host machine.

### 3.2 Interactive security remediation

- **Auto-patch assistance** — after a Trivy scan, offer to generate a patch or an
  updated `Dockerfile` that bumps the base image version to clear critical CVEs.
- **Local SAST** — wire security linters (Gitleaks for secrets, IaC linters)
  directly into the Workspace view.

### 3.3 OCI build and cache analyser

- **Layer visualisation** — analyse a local image and show the size of each
  layer, in the spirit of `dive`. Intended approach:
  - Integrated via `google/go-containerregistry` ("daemonless", no dependency on
    the Docker daemon).
  - Talk to OCI registries directly, pulling manifests and configs without
    downloading the whole image.
  - Stream layers in memory (`tar`) to rebuild the filesystem tree.
  - Compute wasted space by detecting whiteout files (`.wh.`).
- **Cache-miss analysis** — explain why a build's cache was invalidated, e.g.
  "`package.json` changed, invalidating the cache".

### 3.4 Spontaneous dev containers

- **Configuration injection** — inject the developer's dotfiles (vim, zsh,
  aliases) when opening a terminal inside a container.
- **Hot volume mount** — mount the current working directory into a running
  container on the fly, to test a local script without rebuilding the image.

### 3.5 Resource dashboard (embedded mini-htop)

- **TUI charts** — braille-character charts showing live CPU, RAM and network I/O
  for every container in the selected project.
- **Visual alerts** — user-defined thresholds (e.g. memory saturation).

### 3.6 GitHub support alongside GitLab, one active forge per context

Support GitHub as well as GitLab, with **exactly one backend active per
configuration context**. A context targets one forge; switching forge means
switching context.

Not started. The notes below are what the current code imposes on the design,
not a chosen design.

#### What is coupled to GitLab today

| Surface | Size |
|---|---|
| `internal/gitlab` + `internal/ui/gitlab/{auth,explorer}` | ~3 900 lines |
| Direct uses of `*gitlabclient.Client` outside `internal/gitlab` | 66, across 8 files |

The concrete SDK type leaks into `internal/shared/state.go:57`
(`GitLabClient *gitlabclient.Client`), so every consumer is bound to go-gitlab
rather than to a DevDesk abstraction. That field is the load-bearing change: an
interface there is what makes a second forge possible at all.

Also GitLab-shaped: `GitLabConfig` in `internal/config/config.go:41` (URL, token,
clone method, pull settings), the `gitlab-auth` / `gitlab-explorer` view names
and their `gla` / `gle` aliases in `internal/command/parser.go`, and
`shared.GitLabStats`.

#### Model mismatches to settle before coding

These are not implementation details; they decide what the abstraction can even
promise.

- **Nesting.** The explorer is a tree of groups → subgroups → projects. GitHub
  has no nested groups: an organisation holds repositories, flat. Either the
  tree degrades to two levels for GitHub, or the abstraction exposes a depth the
  backend declares.
- **Deletion.** `DeleteGroup` / `DeleteProject` implement GitLab's two-step
  permanent delete (schedule, then purge under the renamed
  `-deletion_scheduled-<id>` path). GitHub deletes immediately and has no
  equivalent, so the "permanent" checkbox is meaningless there — see also D2.
- **Dashboard counters.** `FetchDashboardStats` reads `X-Total` from five list
  endpoints. GitHub has no equivalent header for these; the counts come from the
  search API (`search/issues?q=is:open+is:pr+assignee:@me`), with different rate
  limits and semantics.
- **Vocabulary.** Group/project/merge request vs organisation/repository/pull
  request. The UI must pick per-backend labels or a neutral vocabulary; Rule 129
  applies either way.

#### Open decision: Go SDKs or the `gh` / `glab` CLIs

Worth deciding before any code is written, because it determines whether the
package needs a seam.

Arguments for the CLIs:

- Authentication is already solved, including OAuth device flow, self-hosted
  hosts and token storage. DevDesk's own credential handling could shrink — and
  it has already proven fragile (see §1.1).
- `gh api` and `glab api` are raw REST/GraphQL passthroughs, so no SDK is needed
  for coverage of endpoints the abstraction does not model.
- No SDK version churn to track for two forges.

Arguments against:

- **Per-context isolation conflicts with how these tools store auth.** Both keep
  global per-host state (`~/.config/gh/hosts.yml`). DevDesk contexts want
  *different tokens for the same host*. Driving `gh auth switch` from the TUI
  would mutate the user's global CLI state — the exact mistake avoided in §1.1 by
  scoping `credential.useHttpPath` to the invocation. The clean route is
  `GH_TOKEN` / `GITLAB_TOKEN` per invocation, but then DevDesk still owns the
  tokens and the main benefit is gone.
- **Two more hard dependencies.** Today DevDesk needs `git`, and `docker` only
  for the features that use it. Requiring `gh` and `glab` for the core forge
  feature is a real setup-friction regression.
- **Cost per call.** A process spawn per request, against a reused HTTP
  connection today. The dashboard alone issues five calls, and the explorer
  paginates.
- **Testability regresses.** `internal/gitlab` reaches 100 % with no seam,
  because the SDK takes a base URL that an `httptest` server can stand in for.
  Shelling out would put it back in the position `internal/docker` was in, needing
  a manufactured seam — and stubbed CLI output encodes assumptions about the tool
  rather than testing against it.

**Current recommendation:** keep Go SDKs (go-gitlab, go-github) for the API
surface, and use the CLIs only as an *optional* token source — when a context has
no token, offer to read one from `gh auth token --hostname <host>` or
`glab auth status`. That takes the convenience without the coupling. Recorded as
a recommendation, not a decision.

#### Sketch of the work

1. Define a `forge` abstraction from what the code actually consumes: current
   user, namespace tree, create/delete namespace and repository, initial commit,
   dashboard counters, clone URL.
2. Replace `shared.State.GitLabClient` with that interface. This is the change
   the other 65 call sites follow from.
3. Generalise `GitLabConfig` into a per-context forge config carrying a
   `type: gitlab | github` discriminator, and migrate existing config files.
4. Implement the GitLab backend by moving the existing code behind the
   interface — behaviour-preserving, and covered by the tests added in #7.
5. Implement the GitHub backend.
6. Rename the views and commands, keeping `gla` / `gle` as aliases so muscle
   memory survives.

Steps 1–4 are worth doing on their own: they are a refactor of working code with
tests already in place, and they are what makes step 5 tractable.

---

## 4. Existing plans

Detailed plans live in `.claude/plans/`. One is referenced directly from the old
`todo.md` and is still outstanding:

- [`platform_compatibility_improvements.md`](../.claude/plans/platform_compatibility_improvements.md)
  — Docker-layer platform portability.

12	// DeleteConfirmModal est une boîte de dialogue de confirmation pour suppression
13	// avec option de suppression immédiate
14	type DeleteConfirmModal struct {
15		title             string
16		message           string
17		focused           int  // 0 = checkbox, 1 = Yes, 2 = No
18		permanentlyRemove bool // Si true, suppression immédiate sans période de grâce
19		width             int
20		height            int
21	}
22	
23	// NewDeleteConfirmModal crée une nouvelle modal de confirmation de suppression
24	func NewDeleteConfirmModal(title, message string) *DeleteConfirmModal {
25		return &DeleteConfirmModal{
26			title:             title,
27			message:           message,
28			focused:           2, // Default sur "No" pour éviter les suppressions accidentelles
29			permanentlyRemove: false,
30		}
31	}
32	
33	// NewDeleteConfirmModalPermanent crée une modal avec la case "immediate deletion" pré-cochée et non modifiable.
34	// À utiliser quand le projet est déjà marqué pour suppression — seule la suppression permanente est possible.
35	func NewDeleteConfirmModalPermanent(title, message string) *DeleteConfirmModal {
36		return &DeleteConfirmModal{
37			title:             title,
38			message:           message,
39			focused:           2, // Default sur "No"
40			permanentlyRemove: true,
41		}
42	}
43	
44	// DeleteConfirmModalYesMsg est envoyé quand l'utilisateur confirme la suppression
45	type DeleteConfirmModalYesMsg struct {
46		PermanentlyRemove bool
47	}
48	
49	// DeleteConfirmModalNoMsg est envoyé quand l'utilisateur annule
50	type DeleteConfirmModalNoMsg struct{}
51	
52	// Update met à jour la modal
53	func (m *DeleteConfirmModal) Update(msg tea.Msg) (*DeleteConfirmModal, tea.Cmd) {
54		switch msg := msg.(type) {
55		case tea.WindowSizeMsg:
56			m.width = msg.Width
57			m.height = msg.Height
58	
59		case tea.KeyMsg:
60			switch msg.String() {
61			case "up", "k":
62				// Navigate up
63				if m.focused > 0 {
64					m.focused--
65				}
66				return m, nil
67	
68			case "down", "j":
69				// Navigate down
70				if m.focused < 2 {
71					m.focused++
72				}
73				return m, nil
74	
75			case "left", "h":
76				// Si sur les boutons, aller vers Yes
77				if m.focused == 2 {
78					m.focused = 1
79				}
80				return m, nil
81	
82			case "right", "l":
83				// Si sur les boutons, aller vers No
84				if m.focused == 1 {
85					m.focused = 2
86				}
87				return m, nil
88	
89			case "tab":
90				// Cycle through: checkbox -> Yes -> No -> checkbox
91				m.focused = (m.focused + 1) % 3
92				return m, nil
93	
94			case "shift+tab":
95				// Cycle backwards
96				m.focused = (m.focused + 2) % 3
97				return m, nil
98	
99			case " ":
100				// Toggle checkbox si focus dessus, sinon confirmer la sélection
101				if m.focused == 0 {
102					m.permanentlyRemove = !m.permanentlyRemove
103					return m, nil
104				}
105				return m.handleConfirm()
106	
107			case "enter":
108				return m.handleConfirm()
109	
110			case "y", "Y":
111				// Raccourci pour Yes
112				return m, func() tea.Msg {
113					return DeleteConfirmModalYesMsg{PermanentlyRemove: m.permanentlyRemove}
114				}
115	
116			case "n", "N", "esc":
117				// Raccourci pour No
118				return m, func() tea.Msg {
119					return DeleteConfirmModalNoMsg{}
120				}
121			}
122		}
123	
124		return m, nil
125	}
126	
127	// handleConfirm gère la confirmation selon l'élément sélectionné
128	func (m *DeleteConfirmModal) handleConfirm() (*DeleteConfirmModal, tea.Cmd) {
129		switch m.focused {
130		case 0:
131			// Toggle checkbox
132			m.permanentlyRemove = !m.permanentlyRemove
133			return m, nil
134		case 1:
135			// Yes
136			return m, func() tea.Msg {
137				return DeleteConfirmModalYesMsg{PermanentlyRemove: m.permanentlyRemove}
138			}
139		case 2:
140			// No
141			return m, func() tea.Msg {
142				return DeleteConfirmModalNoMsg{}
143			}
144		}
145		return m, nil
146	}
147	
148	// View affiche la modal
149	func (m *DeleteConfirmModal) View() string {
150		var b strings.Builder
151	
152		// Titre
153		b.WriteString(theme.TitleStyle.Render(m.title))
154		b.WriteString("\n\n")
155	
156		// Message
157		b.WriteString(m.message)
158		b.WriteString("\n\n")
159	
160		// Checkbox pour suppression immédiate
161		checkboxStyle := lipgloss.NewStyle().Background(theme.ColorBackground)
162		if m.focused == 0 {
163			checkboxStyle = checkboxStyle.Bold(true).Foreground(theme.ColorHighlight)
164		}
165	
166		checkbox := theme.IconCheckbox
167		if m.permanentlyRemove {
168			checkbox = theme.IconChecked
169		}
170	
171		indicator := "  "
172		if m.focused == 0 {
173			indicator = theme.IconCircleSmall + " "
174		}
175	
176		checkboxLabel := " Immediate deletion (no grace period)"
177		checkboxLine := checkboxStyle.Render(indicator + checkbox + checkboxLabel)
178		b.WriteString(checkboxLine)
179	
180		// Warning si suppression immédiate activée
181		if m.permanentlyRemove {
182			b.WriteString("\n")
183			warningStyle := lipgloss.NewStyle().Background(theme.ColorBackground).Foreground(theme.ColorHighlight).Italic(true)
184			b.WriteString(warningStyle.Render("  " + theme.IconWarning + " This action is irreversible!"))
185		}
186		b.WriteString("\n\n")
187	
188		// Boutons
189		yes := theme.RenderButton("Yes", m.focused == 1, "danger")
190		no := theme.RenderButton("No", m.focused == 2, "primary")
191	
192		buttons := yes + theme.Bg("  ") + no
193		b.WriteString(buttons)
194		b.WriteString("\n\n")
195	
196		return lipgloss.NewStyle().
197			Background(theme.ColorBackground).
198			Foreground(theme.ColorText).
199			Border(lipgloss.NormalBorder()).
200			BorderForeground(theme.ColorError).
201			BorderBackground(theme.ColorBackground).
202			Padding(1, 2).
203			Render(b.String())
204	}
